Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Krishna explains that the four functional divisions of human society were created by Him according to inherent qualities and actions, yet He remains transcendental to these divisions as the non-doer.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Understanding social order, individual psychophysical natures, and divine detachment.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna clarifies: 'catur-varnyam maya srstam guna-karma-vibhagasah, tasya kartaram api mam viddhy akartaram avyayamy' (The four social divisions were created by Me according to quality and work; know Me to be the non-doer and unchangeable despite creating it).
Outcome/Resolution: Defines social roles based on natural inclination (guna) and aptitude (karma), while demonstrating divine transcendence.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Personality Types and Aptitude Alignment: Matching work and duties to one's natural traits and abilities
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Role Detachment: Fulfilling functional societal roles without reducing self-worth to them
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Authentic Self-Expression: Living in harmony with one's intrinsic psychological nature

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Catur-varnyam maya srstam guna-karma-vibhagasah (Four divisions created according to quality and action)
Kartaram api mam viddhy akartaram (Creator yet remaining the non-doer)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Social order is structured around natural psychological qualities (gunas) and duties (karma), yet God remains entirely unattached and transcendental to these material structures.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Aligning your work with your natural personality traits promotes harmony, while maintaining inner detachment prevents societal roles from defining your entire sense of self.
